title: Oil crashed 13%, tech sold off and jobs blew past forecasts
dek: Democrats swept the midterms and stocks rallied Wednesday. Then AI regulation fears crushed chips, Brent fell about 13% on the week, and a hot jobs report lifted December hike odds.
summary: A midterm relief rally, Thursday's AI selloff, oil's steep weekly drop, and a much stronger October jobs report. Plus Apple, AMD and Qualcomm earnings, and the week ahead.
keyNumbersNote: Nov 6 close, change since Oct 30 close

briefs.headline: Democrats sweep, Dow surges
briefs.body: Democrats took majorities in the House and Senate, plus key governor races including Texas. Trump said he accepted the results. On Wednesday the Dow rose 1,569 points, or 3.0%, to 53,356, its best day since April 2025, and Brent fell nearly 9% to about $95 as markets priced a softer Iran stance.

briefs.headline: Tech's worst day since April
briefs.body: Thursday erased that rally and more. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% into correction, the S&P 500 about 4.4% and the Dow about 3.4%, each the worst session since April 2025. The Magnificent Seven lost more than $1 trillion, Nvidia alone more than $440 billion, and the chip index dropped about 12%.

briefs.headline: Oil's steepest week in months
briefs.body: January Brent settled Friday at $98.32, down about 13% on the week and 16% from the Oct 30 close of $117.64. WTI settled at $90.83. Reports tied the move to midterm hopes of a US-Iran settlement, even as tanker attacks in the Gulf continued.

briefs.headline: Jobs crush the forecast
briefs.body: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, far above forecasts near 60,000, and unemployment slipped to 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year. Traders lifted December Fed hike odds to about 77%.

briefs.headline: Data centers become political
briefs.body: Voters sided against data centers in 38 of 39 fully counted local ballot measures. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa pledged a new-permit moratorium. Dan Ives said 10% to 20% of planned US AI sites could be delayed or scrapped, and Goldman Sachs flagged about 45% of planned capacity at risk of temporary freezes.

briefs.headline: BoE hikes, ISM stays hot
briefs.body: The Bank of England raised its rate 25 bp to 4.00%, the first hike since 2023, in an 8 to 1 vote. US ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5, while services eased to 54.5. Australia's cash rate moved to 4.85%.

earningsLead: Beats did not clear the AI overhang. Apple warned on margins, AMD guided strong, Qualcomm guided soft.

earnings.line: Revenue $114.48B, up 12%, EPS $2.10. Gross margin 47.9%; December guide 45% to 46% on memory and Siri AI costs. Stock down about 2% after the call.
Revenue $13.38B; data center $8.55B, up 97%. Guided Q4 revenue about $17B and 2027 growth above 80%. Stock jumped after hours, then swung with the chip selloff.
Non-GAAP revenue $10.44B and EPS $2.17. Soft Q1 EPS guide midpoint. Stock fell more than 9% Thursday with the chip rout.
Revenue $2.31B, up 96%. US commercial $984M topped US government for the first time. Raised 2026 revenue guide to $8.53B.

items: China October inflation. Occidental, Take-Two and Rocket Lab report.
October CPI at 8:30 AM. CoreWeave reports after the close. Anthropic IPO marketing may begin.
Veterans Day; US bond market closed, stocks open.
Jobless claims and existing home sales. Nebius before the open; Applied Materials and Cisco after the close.
